new_exact_v1_reviews.title: AgentWall: A Runtime Safety Layer for Local AI Agents
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: The safety of autonomous AI agents is increasingly recognized as a critical open problem.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: Existing AI safety work has focused primarily on model alignment and input filtering, but these approaches do not address what happens at the moment an agent's intent becomes a real action on a real machine.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: We present the design, architecture, threat model, and policy model of AgentWall, and demonstrate 92.9% policy enforcement accuracy with sub-millisecond overhead across 14 benchmark tests.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: We present the design, architecture, threat model, and policy model of AgentWall, and demonstrate 92.9% policy enforcement accuracy with sub-millisecond overhead across 14 benchmark tests.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: We present the design, architecture, threat model, and policy model of AgentWall, show its effectiveness across representative local-agent safety scenarios, and discuss its limitations and relationship to complementary safety approaches.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.
